title: Waterfall interaction edge cases + accessibility draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a set of interaction edge cases, accessibility considerations, and small-wireframe notes for the waterfall/trace viewer. It is intentionally lightweight — meant to surface problems we keep hitting in QA and during usability sessions, propose lightweight fixes, and create a grooming checklist for the backlog.

High-level goals:
- Make waterfall interactions robust for large and tiny traces (1 span -> 10k spans).
- Support keyboard-first navigation and screen-reader semantics for span focus and context.
- Reduce visual jank when zooming and resizing timelines (esp. on low-end GPUs).
- Provide deterministic filter + pinning semantics for multi-select and persistent filters.

Quick problem inventory (observed in QA / support):
1) Zoom jitter when jumping to a span at extreme time scales
   - Repro: open trace with long idle region, use zoom-to-span on a span near the end. Timeline briefly renders multiple widths then snaps.
   - Impact: feels glitchy; hard to orient.
   - Suspected cause: layout recalcs triggered by async measurement of label widths + dynamic scrollbar width.

2) Keyboard focus doesn't preserve horizontal offset
   - Tab/arrow moves focus to next span, but the timeline view recenters differently compared to click interaction.
   - Accessibility issue: VoiceOver users lose context when focus jumps to a span off-screen.

3) Grouped spans collapse state lost after filter change
   - If user collapses a host/operation group, applies filter, then clears filter, expansion state is not preserved.
   - Expected: remember collapsed/expanded state per-trace session (or per-capture) unless user explicitly toggles.

4) Massive traces -> expensive repaint when hover tooltip renders detailed headers
   - Tooltip shows full attributes for span on hover and triggers synchronous layout reads.
   - Solution sketch: render lightweight tooltip first, then lazily populate details. Use requestIdleCallback for non-blocking attribute fetch.

5) Filter scripting language ambiguity
   - Users can write quick filter expressions (e.g., status != 200 && duration > 50). Current syntax is case-sensitive; error messages are terse.
   - UX ask: make errors actionable and add inline examples + live linting.

Wireframe/interaction notes (quick sketches described in words):
- Zoom handle behavior:
  - Two modes: smooth and snap. Smooth is continuous pinch/scroll. Snap aligns to major time ticks (1s, 100ms, 10ms) when user crosses velocity threshold.
  - Micro-suggestion: when snapping, fade-in a small hint: "Zoom snapped to 100ms resolution" for 1s.

- Keyboard navigation model:
  - Left/Right arrows: move focus to previous/next visible span. Shift+Left/Right: expand selection (for multi-select).
  - Enter: open span detail panel. Escape: close.
  - Home/End: jump to first/last visible span.
  - PageUp/PageDown: pan timeline horizontally by visible width.
  - When focus moves to a span off view, we should animate scroll with reduced motion option honored.

- Screen reader semantics:
  - Each span element should expose name, start offset (ms), duration (ms), and a short attribute summary via aria-label.
  - Interaction hint (e.g., "Press Enter for details") should be appended to focused span announcement.

- Filter pinning and persistence:
  - Pin toggle in the filter bar persists filters across trace loads for the session. Pinned filters appear as a subtle bar above timeline.
  - When a pinned filter is active and user applies a temporary quick-filter, show combined chip: "pinned:status=500 + temp:duration>200" with an easy clear X for temp.

Accessibility / reduced motion / low-power mode notes:
- Provide a system-wide reduced motion toggle that disables timeline easing/animated pan/hover fades. Respect system prefers-reduced-motion.
- Low-power mode (heuristic based on CPU/GPU or explicit user toggle) should: reduce render frequency during scrubbing (throttle to 30fps), hide non-essential animations, and switch to simplified SVG/Canvas fallback for spans.

Performance edge cases and quick mitigations:
- 5k+ spans: virtualize rows + aggregate spans with identical start windows into glyph clusters. Show a heatmap icon with count and on hover expand cluster.
- When painting on canvas, avoid expensive shadow/blur props; use solid shapes for cluster glyphs.
- Debounce tooltip data fetches by 100ms; if pointer moves more than 10px ignore.

Interaction tolerance and hit targets:
- Expand click target of a small-duration span (less than 3px) to a minimum interactive width of 12px for pointer and keyboard focus.
- When several tiny spans overlap visually, use a stacked hover menu that lists overlapping spans in chronological order. Keyboard navigation moves through stacked list with Up/Down.

Unresolved questions / gating items for grooming:
- How aggressively do we want to preserve grouping expansion state across filters vs. clearing state? (product tradeoff: predictability vs. surprise)
- Do we add a lightweight filter language helper in the primary UI or keep it in an "advanced filter" drawer?
- What is acceptable animation budget for low-end GPUs? We need SRE/infra guidance for metrics to detect GPU slowness client-side.

Backlog grooming proposals (PRIORITIZE):
1) PROD-3421: Zoom snap + reduced motion option (M). Acceptance: no jitter repro 95th percentile after impl, tests for snap thresholds.
2) Accessibility keyboard nav overhaul (H). Acceptance: pass a11y audit for keyboard and screen-reader flows (NVDA + VoiceOver).
3) Filter pinning persistence UX (M). Acceptance: pinned filters survive trace navigation and are visible in UI.
4) Tooltip lazy hydration (M). Acceptance: initial hover paint < 10ms, full details load deferred.
5) Cluster glyphs for >2k spans (L).

QA checklist (quick):
- [ ] Reproduce zoom jitter on staging (trace id: sample-long-id-001).
- [ ] Verify keyboard focus always announces span aria-labels.
- [ ] Test pinned filters persist across traces on same session.
- [ ] Run perf budget on 2k/5k traces on low-end VM.
- [ ] Validate tooltip hydration does not block main thread.

Notes to design/engineering collaboration:
- Marco: can you prototype the snap hint micro-copy + reduced motion toggle? Link to the prototype in linked_artifacts when ready.
- Lena: please draft the aria-label templates for span elements (short, mid, verbose) so we can ship a user-configurable verbosity level.
- Owen: add a small telemetry flag to trace viewer that reports client-side dropped frames during interactions (opt-in). We can use this to gate low-power heuristics.

Appendix: quick micro copy examples (for UI):
- Zoom hint: "Zoom aligned to 100ms resolution"
- Pinned filter chip: "Pinned: status = 500"
- Tooltip skeleton: "Loading details…"

This doc is a working draft — use comments below for small additions. After grooming we should split into individual tickets per area and attach small acceptance tests.

-- Aisha
